decisions.issues: Minor only: the column is already marching out through the burnt gap rather than standing in ranks; the charred two-post frame at right is just stockade timber (no rope or noose). Brown marks on breeches read as soot and scorch, not blood. Wide open sky across the top for both captions.

Minor only: the Nair mundus fall to mid-calf with red borders rather than reading as short, and the Dutch around him are bare-headed (1.2 does not require hats). De Lannoy matches his sheet (pale curly hair with black ribbon), wears a torn, soot-stained blue coat, and the bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist. His sword is sheathed and his eyes are on the Nair line. Hands are sound and there is no text. The open sky across the upper centre and right gives room for both captions.

Minor only: Nagoji's tunic sleeves are rolled to mid-forearm, which the panel does not specify. The brand is not visible because the inner left forearm faces away, so nothing on him contradicts the bible. Dhanaji is frame-left and shorter and stockier, with white pagdi, short black beard, indigo quilted tunic, no sash and talwar, on a brown horse. Nagoji is frame-right with rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN chin, tiny gold ear stud, cream tunic, red sash, boots and talwar. Kayal is a red-brown bay with black mane and no white markings. The waiting riders and matchlock muzzle sit in the dune hollow at upper left, and there is no text. Dhanaji's balloons fit in the sky and palm space at about x 0.22 to 0.52, y 0.01 to 0.19, above his turban and left of Nagoji's head, without covering the hidden riders at the far upper left.

Minor: framed as a waist-up medium shot rather than a true close-up. Sleeves are rolled up, so the brand and long white scar show. They are correctly on his inner LEFT forearm, drawn as a puckered patch with no letters and no cross, which fits the ch13-15 bible row and the sheet's rolled sleeves, although the panel text did not ask for them. Light stipple shading on the chin reads as skin texture, not a beard. The ear ornament reads as a small gold stud on the lobe. A collapsed canvas in the burnt camp is wreckage, not a standing tent. Large open sky at upper right for the balloon.

Minor: the camera sits at sand level on the crest of the rise rather than well below it, so the shot is only slightly low-angle. Varma matches his sheet (black hair, cream-and-gold turban with peacock crest, gold necklaces, spear upright, no crown). A Nair at his side holds a white conch at his hip. Nair lines with round shields and spears flank the path down to the burnt camp. No text needed.

Minor: framing is a medium shot rather than tight, the conch blower's cheeks are not visibly puffed, and the background is not soft-focused; a few other Dutch soldiers are still moving in the camp, though the foreground soldier clearly steps clear of a charred post. Nair carries a brass-hilted sword at the hip. No text, gore or anatomy faults; setting (beach, burnt stockade, distant ships) matches the page.

Minor: Nair firearms read more like flintlocks than matchlocks; shields are medium rather than small; one Dutch soldier sits on the sand beside the column (no blood, reads as halted/exhausted) and a figure behind him wears a dark brownish coat, tiny at reading size. Beat is clear: bare-chested Nair gunners in white mundus on the dunes, mounted riders among them, shield-and-spear line closing, small blue-coated Dutch column in the middle, no text.

Minor: De Lannoy's LEFT hand and wrist carry the linen bandage as required, but his right wrist also shows a white wrap that could read as a second bandage; Donnadi holds a drawn brass-hilted sword while a second brass-hilted sword hangs scabbarded at his left hip. Otherwise matches: De Lannoy tall, pale curly hair with ribbon, torn soot-stained blue coat, sword sheathed, standing still; Donnadi shorter, stocky, dark hair tied back, sashed blue coat, shouting and pointing toward the blocked road. Clear sky at top for the caption.

Minor: Donnadi has a fuller short beard here than the heavy stubble in panel 3, but he still reads as the same man (stocky, dark hair tied back, sashed gold-trimmed blue coat, brass-hilted sword raised, face in rage). Large clear sky upper right for both balloons.

Minor: the quiet space directly above the heads at frame-left is palm fronds, so the two whisper balloons should sit in the open sky just right of De Lannoy's head (top centre). The bandaged hand on Donnadi's shoulder reads as De Lannoy's LEFT hand (index on top, little finger at the bottom, back of hand to camera).

Clean enough to use. Ramayyan is on-model: thin, bare-headed, receding curly black hair, plain unbordered white cloth, no marks or jewellery. He sits on a brown horse at frame-left and lowers an open, palm-down hand toward the bare sand in front of the standing Dutch rank. The Dutch are at the right edge, faces turned away, with blue coats, buff cuffs and upright muskets, so the round-1 beat problem is fixed. The Nair spearmen are bare-chested. There is no painted text. Minor points: his horse has a white blaze, while the horse in 3.1 has none (this is not Kayal, so it is tolerable), and the arm still angles outward a little more than a pure drop from the elbow. The open sky in the upper centre between Ramayyan and the Dutch has room for both balloons.

Clean. This is the tight hands-only insert the script asks for, with no faces anywhere. Dutch hands in blue sleeves with buff, brass-buttoned cuffs (matching the soldiers in 3.3) clench upright flintlocks. In the centre, Donnadi's hand grips the brass hilt of his sheathed sword, against the gold-edged blue officer's coat and crimson sash he wears in 3.2. Hands and fingers are sound, and there is no painted text. Minor: the arm just right of the hilt, holding a musket, has a buff cuff, so it reads as a neighbouring soldier rather than Donnadi's own left arm. The hands grip the fore-stocks and barrels rather than the butts. The large open sky in the upper right holds both captions easily.

v03 is clean. Nagoji matches the commander sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic with full-length sleeves (so no brand shows, which is correct for this panel), broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, brass-hilted sword, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and a small flush gold ear stud. Kayal is a bay with a black mane and no white markings, and her lower legs are cropped out of frame. The setting is right for the beat: the burnt stockade on the sand, the sandy battery rise with a cannon and bare-chested Nair spearmen in white mundus, palms, and Dutch ships small on the sea under clear morning light. There is no painted text, no gore and no anachronism, and the hands are sound. The upper-right sky is wide and empty, with room for the medium caption. One small nitpick: one or two of the tiny background workers at bottom right may have a dark head-cloth, which can't be read at print size. v02 and v01 both paint the brand on Nagoji's raised forearm. That is his far arm, the RIGHT one, not the left, and the brand shows even though the script does not push his sleeves up. Neither is a valid backup.

Minor: Donnadi's hair reads as loose rather than clearly tied back, and he has stubble where other panels give him a short beard. Otherwise clean. The round spyglass vignette sits in a black surround, he looks up at the sky with his lips parted, and the uniform and brass hilt are correct. There is clear sky inside the top of the circle, and black corners, for the caption.

Minor: Donnadi has a fuller short beard and a mustard waist sash, a little different from his look on page 3. The beat is clear: a thin drummer boy in an oversized blue coat grips his drumsticks, Donnadi's hand rests on his shoulder, and the boy lifts his chin with wet eyes and pressed lips. The hands are sound and there is a large open sky at upper right for the caption.

Minor only. Donnadi's men are drawn slumped and seated among the charred timbers, not standing and swaying. Some Nair spearmen are bearded and look older than the bible's 'young' guards. Otherwise clean: Donnadi is shorter and stocky, dark hair tied back, sashed blue coat, brass hilt in hand. De Lannoy is tall and pale-haired, in a torn, soot-stained blue coat and boots, with the bandage on his LEFT hand. They lock eyes, with the Nair spear ring at right and the burnt camp on the beach. Hands are sound and there is no text. There is open sky at upper left for the oath balloon.

Minor: the shot includes Donnadi's face, so it is looser than the 'Tight. hands' direction, and he wears a maroon cross-sash. The hands are anatomically sound and hold the unbuckled belt with its sheathed sword. His thumb is on the brass guard, which has interlaced knotwork with no letters, and the metal catches the sun. There is wide clear sky at upper right for the long caption.

Minor. Donnadi's red sash (seen in 4.3) is cropped out above the frame. A cream cloth (shirt tail or lining) hangs at his hip, which is harmless. The rest fits the beat: a sand-level view of the sheathed brass-hilted sword and belt in the sand, with sand puffs still settling. Only Donnadi's boots and the lower part of his blue coat show, with no face, so he can speak from off panel. Behind him the Dutch column waits in tricorns and blue coats, and bare-chested Nair spearmen stand on the dune. The beach and burnt stockade match 4.3. The hilt's openwork scrolls carry no letters. There is clear sky at upper left for the caption and open sky at top centre for Donnadi's off-panel 'Down.' balloon.

Clean on the script beat: blue-coated column, muskets lying on the sand, weeping and rigid men, drum set down with the drummer boy behind it, sergeant kneeling with his forehead to his musket, Nair guards on the dune, burnt stockade and distant ships, no text. Minor: the tall fair-haired soldier gazing upward at left centre loosely echoes De Lannoy (who is meant to be off-panel) but has golden-brown loose hair, no ribboned queue, no bandage and an untorn coat, so he reads as an ordinary soldier; the kneeling sergeant still carries a pistol and hanger on his belt. Caption sits well in the open sky at upper right.

Varma matches his sheet and the beach rule for pages 1 to 7: cream-and-gold turban with jewelled peacock-feather crest, black hair, curled moustache, pearl ear drop, gold necklaces and armlets, bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth, spear butt grounded on the battery rise beside a cannon, calm stance. Minor: a few small embers still glow among the charred posts at lower right and a collapsed canvas lies in the ruined camp (not a standing tent); the prisoners are off-panel. Large clear sky to the right of his head for the balloon.

Shows the beat: disarmed European prisoners walking a red earth road between palms and paddy, hands free with no ropes, bare-chested Nair guards in white mundus with small round shields and spears on both flanks, sea out of view, Udayagiri's walls and bastions on the green hill ahead, no text. Minor: the prisoners have shed their blue coats and tricorns (shirts, waistcoats and breeches only), a costume step away from 5.1, though the caption identifies them; the guards' topknots sit on the crown rather than tied forward; a few prisoners wear thong sandals. Open sky across the top centre and top right takes both captions.

v03 is the newest version and it is acceptable. De Lannoy matches his sheet: pale curly hair tied with a black ribbon, face in profile tilted up, the only upright head. He wears the torn, soot-stained blue coat, and the linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist (the near hand, on screen right). The prisoners around him are dark-haired Europeans with bowed heads, and Nair guards (topknots, white mundus, round shields, spears) walk on both flanks. Udayagiri's granite walls and bastions fill the background behind and above him. No painted text, noose, blood or anachronism, and the hands are sound. Clear sky for the caption sits top right, above his head (about x 0.46 to 0.94, y 0.01 to 0.13). Small faults for the author: (1) the prisoners wear knee boots, but in 5.3 they walk barefoot or in sandals; (2) several bowed prisoners share the same bearded face; (3) his body is turned three-quarters toward the viewer, so only his head is a strict profile. Why the others lost: v02 has two more blond, pale-haired prisoners, which breaks 'the only tall, pale-haired Dutchman'. v01 shows Indian-looking prisoners in turbans and dhotis and no Nair guards, which does not match 5.3.

Acceptable. Minor: Nagoji's rolled sleeves (as on the commander sheet) expose the brand on his inner LEFT forearm, drawn as a pale looped scar patch with the thin scar running toward the wrist (correct arm, no letters, reads as scar tissue at page size); his right forearm is clean. Ibrahim's LEFT ear-to-jaw scar is on the correct side but slightly reddish rather than pale. Ibrahim's gaze goes up and to frame-left rather than toward the wrecked camp on the right, and Nagoji walks along the shore rather than down off a dune. Nagoji's gold ornament is a small bead at the lobe that reads as a stud. Open sky top-left and top-centre holds the caption and both balloons clear of faces.

Acceptable. The r1 fixes worked. Ibrahim is barefoot, as when he stepped ashore in 6.1. His head turns toward frame-left, where Nagoji stands off-panel, while his LEFT arm sweeps an open palm across the burned stockade, rope, metal and torn canvas. The thin scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw is on the visible, correct side, though it is slightly reddish rather than pale. Hands are sound. Smoke still rises from the stockade, which fits the morning after. The open sky top-left and top-centre holds all three balloons clear of his face and hand. Nagoji's off-panel tail goes to the left edge.

v03 is a light re-pass of v02 (same composition, mean pixel difference small), and it is clean enough for print. Ibrahim matches his sheet: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over a cream vest with pocket flaps. He gestures toward the goods, and his crew unloads the second boat behind him. Nagoji matches the commander sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red waist sash, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny gold stud. His hand is in the open rice sack and his eyes look down and to his right, toward the sacks. The setting matches 6.1 and 6.2: Colachel surf, small open boats, the charred stockade and debris up the beach, morning light. There is no painted text, gore or noose, and the hands are sound. There is open sky top-left (x 0 to 0.55, y 0 to 0.14) for Ibrahim's two balloons and sky top-centre or top-right for Nagoji's short one. Minor faults: (1) Nagoji's sleeves are rolled to the elbow although the script does not ask for it, so his brand and the long white scar show. They sit on the upper or outer face of the LEFT forearm rather than the inner face. The brand reads as a slightly lace-like ridged patch, with no letters and no cross. (2) Nagoji's downward glance could also read as falling on Ibrahim's lower hand, but most readers will take it as the sacks. (3) The scarred side of Ibrahim's face is turned away, which is consistent, but the scar cannot be seen here.
decisions.correction: No retouch is needed for acceptance. Optionally, soften the lace-like pattern of the brand on Nagoji's left forearm into a blurred, puckered pale patch, at roughly x 0.80 to 0.87, y 0.40 to 0.52 of the v03 frame.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The r1 fix worked: Ibrahim faces frame-right, and his visible RIGHT cheek and jaw are now unmarked. It is a face-to-face medium two-shot at the waterline. Ibrahim is unsmiling and taps his chest with two fingers, and his hands are sound. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, flush gold stud, rust-red turban, red sash, talwar at his left hip. His brand and thin white scar are on the LEFT forearm only, with the sleeve rolled as in 6.1, and his right forearm is clean. Minor: a tiny dot on Ibrahim's right earlobe reads as a small piercing that is not on his sheet, but it is barely visible. The open sky upper-left takes both of Ibrahim's balloons clear of the faces.

Acceptable. The r1 fixes worked. Nagoji, in the left foreground from behind, has his left hand on his hip beside the talwar at his left hip. His RIGHT forearm, hanging at frame-right, is clean, and his lost profile shows the moustache, clean chin and flush gold stud. Ibrahim is thigh-deep in the surf heading out toward the boats on the right. His body is three-quarters turned away and he looks back over his LEFT shoulder, grinning and waving, with the shawl on his left shoulder as on his sheet. Minor: at this small scale the thin scar on his visible left cheek is not drawn. The stockade at the top-left edge still smoulders with small embers, which fits the morning after. There is no painted text, and the wide open sky over the boats at upper right takes the caption, with sky above and left of Ibrahim for his long balloon.

The runner is missing. Ramayyan holds out the palm-leaf message himself instead of receiving it from a panting runner. With the caption, the beat (news arriving while Varma watches the sea) still reads. Nagoji's sleeves are rolled, so the brand and scar show on his inner LEFT forearm. That is the correct arm and the correct form, as on his sheet. Ramayyan's white cloth has a few brown dirt spots that do not read as blood. Varma (crested turban, spear, necklaces) and Nagoji (clean-shaven chin, flush stud) are on model. A large clear sky at the upper right holds the caption and Varma's balloon.

Minor: Dhanaji is already seated in the saddle rather than caught mid-swing into it. Varma's moustache is a little fuller than the bible's thin waxed line, but the namam, pearl drops and peacock crest keep him distinct from Nagoji. Varma has a faint reddish graze on one cheek (no blood). Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny gold stud. He wears the rust-red turban and red sash, and no brand is shown. Dhanaji matches his sheet: white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, brown horse. Both principals sit behind Varma, who points down the coast across the burnt stockade under clear sky. Open sky upper right (x 0.65-1.0, y 0-0.22) takes Varma's balloon, and the sky between the turbans (x 0.40-0.50, y 0-0.10) or the upper middle takes Dhanaji's. No painted text.

Nagoji's ear ornament reads as a tiny gold ring rather than a flush stud. It is minor at this scale. With one hand pressed to his ribs, he holds no reins, which suits the beat. Otherwise the panel is on model. Kayal is bay with a black mane and black lower legs and no white marks. Dhanaji wears a white pagdi and indigo tunic on his brown horse. The Madurai lancers wear white turbans and jamas and carry plain lances. The palms form a blurred wall. The open sky at the upper right holds the caption.

Minor: the Dutch fire from behind a palm-log barricade rather than standing caught on open wet sand. Nagoji charges toward the left rather than clearly wheeling away. Otherwise the beat is clear. Kayal reads as a bay with black mane, tail and lower legs and no white markings. Nagoji has a clean-shaven chin, thick curled moustache, gold stud, rust-red turban and red sash. Dhanaji rides a brown horse, with a beard, white pagdi and indigo quilted tunic, and charges at the Dutch with the scouts in white behind him. The Dutch wear blue coats and tricorns with fixed bayonets, and their volley smoke blows back into the front man's face. There are no wounds, no red coats and no painted text. Large open sky at the upper right (x 0.58-1.0, y 0-0.22) holds both captions.

There is a faint pale scar line on Nagoji's RIGHT (sword) forearm that the bible does not call for. It is small at reading scale and could be retouched. The runner sits at the lower left, so his balloon's tail must run down from the sky past Nagoji's sword arm. The beat is otherwise right. Nagoji is reined in on Kayal (solid bay, no white) with the talwar held across his chest. The runner at his stirrup holds a plain palm-leaf message. The Dutch in blue coats and tricorns, bayonets fixed, fall back into the haze, with the red-sashed officer limping between two men. A large clear sky at the upper right holds the four lettering lines.

Minor only. Tharakan wears two crosses on two chains, not one, and a tiny ear stud that is not on his sheet. Both are small at this wide framing. Everything else matches: Nagoji at the door has the rust-red turban, red sash and talwar, a thick curled moustache, clean chin and a flush gold stud. Varma is bare-headed with his side knot on the left, the namam and pearl drops, and his spear within reach. Ramayyan has his stylus and palm leaves, the window shows green hills and the drilling yard, and the lamp is brass. The caption fits on the plain stone wall at upper centre (x 0.30 to 0.60, y 0.02 to 0.20).

Minor. The platform under the window is empty (Varma is implied off-panel to the left) and holds a rolled mat where panel 1 has red bolsters. De Lannoy matches his sheet (pale curly hair, ribbon), with the bandage correctly on his LEFT hand. He wears the torn blue coat and boots, does not bow, and has a bare-chested Nair spear guard on each side. The balloon fits on the plain wall at upper left-centre (x 0.28 to 0.55, y 0.0 to 0.30).

v03 is nearly clean. The framing is right: we look past De Lannoy's back (pale curled hair with a black ribbon, torn and soot-stained blue coat, bandage on his LEFT hand) at Varma seated on the low platform. Varma rests one forearm on his knee and looks up. He is bare-headed with the knot above his left ear, wears his pearl earrings and gold beads, and his spear leans within reach. The window shows green hills and Nair spearmen drilling. There is no painted text. The upper wall between the spear and the door, above Varma's head, gives plenty of room for both balloons. Minor: the room is mirrored against 8.5 (window left and door right here; door left and window right in 8.5). It reads as a reverse angle and does not need a fix. Rejected alternatives: v02 has the bandage on De Lannoy's RIGHT hand (seen from behind). v01 gives Varma loose wavy hair with no side knot.

v03 matches the beat: a two-shot across the room. De Lannoy stands with his mouth open, in the torn blue coat, breeches and boots, his bandaged LEFT hand held out. Varma sits in left profile with one hand lifted, bare-headed with the knot above his left ear, his earring and gold beads showing, and his spear leaning beside him. There is no painted text. A large blank granite wall between and above the two heads leaves room for Varma's balloon to overlap De Lannoy's. Remaining faults: (1) A long hanging object at De Lannoy's belt (about x 0.15 to 0.18, y 0.40 to 0.58) reads as a sheathed dagger or empty scabbard. That is odd on a disarmed prisoner, though small at print size. (2) The room is mirrored against 8.4 (door left and window right here). (3) A few distant drillers in the window wear white headbands instead of forward topknots, too small to matter. (4) A bolster on the platform is fine (not a carpet or throne). Rejected alternatives: v02 has the bandage on De Lannoy's RIGHT (near, hanging) hand. v01 dresses De Lannoy in the white tunic-coat and mundu, which is the wrong costume before 13.4.
decisions.correction: Optional local retouch: paint out the narrow brown hanging scabbard or dagger shape below De Lannoy's belt on his left hip (roughly x 0.15 to 0.18, y 0.40 to 0.58 of the frame). Replace it with the dark grey breeches and the blue coat edge so he reads as unarmed. Nothing else needs changing.

decisions.issues: Clean. Varma matches his sheet: black hair, bare-headed, no turban or crest, cream and gold mundu, gold necklaces. He leans forward with his right hand resting on the spear shaft. The setting matches: granite walls, platform, mats, timber door, a brass lamp with an open wick, and the window onto the yard with bare-chested Nair drillers. The side knot sits on the far, hidden side of his head, which is fine. The upper wall between the window and the door (about x 0.52-0.80, y 0.02-0.32) is clear for both balloons. De Lannoy is off panel to the right, where Varma is looking.

Acceptable. Varma's hair is jet black now, in a sleek knot on his visible LEFT side as on the sheet's left profile. He is bare-headed and bare-chested, in a cream mundu with a gold border and plain gold bead necklaces, with no cross. He sits on the stone platform with his spear leaning within reach. Tharakan has grey receding hair, a fine grey moustache and a clean chin, with maroon silk under heavy gold chains, and he gestures softly with open hands. The setting matches: plain timber door, granite walls, a woven mat, a brass lamp with open wicks, no table, and a window onto the hills and the drilling spearmen. Hands are sound and there is no painted text. Minor issues: Tharakan's cross is a plain Latin cross with only slightly flared ends, not budded. Varma's earring is a gold ball, not a pearl drop. His moustache is a little fuller than the bible's thin waxed one. Lettering space: grey wall above Tharakan's head (top-left, x 0.08 to 0.47, y 0.02 to 0.19) and wall above Varma (x 0.66 to 0.95, y 0.0 to 0.11).

v03 is clean on the hard checks and matches the beat. The shot is over De Lannoy's shoulder (pale hair with the black ribbon, torn soot-stained blue coat, linen bandage on his LEFT hand, standing). Varma is bare-headed with the side knot above his left ear, namam, pearl drops and thin waxed moustache, and his eyes are on De Lannoy. Tharakan sits at right in the maroon tunic with lit gold chains and a cross. The open window shows green hills and spearmen drilling in the yard. The lamp is brass with an open wick. No text, and the upper stone wall between De Lannoy's head and the window (about x 0.40 to 0.80, y 0.02 to 0.25) is clear for both Varma balloons. Minor remaining points for the author: (1) An extra, unscripted bare-chested guard stands by the door at far left. He has a thick curled moustache, a gold ear stud and loose curly hair with no topknot, so a reader could take him for Nagoji without his rust-red turban and sash. (2) Tharakan's cross is a plain Latin cross with only slightly flared ends, not clearly the budded St Thomas form. It is not a crucifix. (3) Varma's nod toward Tharakan is barely visible: his head is almost upright, though his gaze reads correctly. Backup v02 is the same composition, but Varma wears a small gold cross pendant on his lower necklace, which is a hard identity fault.
decisions.correction: No retouch is needed for the pick. Optional local retouch: if the door guard at far left (about x 0.00 to 0.09, y 0.10 to 0.65 of v03) reads as Nagoji, paint his loose curls into a forward-tied Nair topknot and remove the gold ear stud at about x 0.067, y 0.24. Alternatively, paint him out entirely, filling with the dark doorway and the timber door frame.

decisions.issues: Acceptable. The tight insert shows a weathered hand from a plain white-clad figure laying a water-stained folded letter with a broken red wax seal on the woven mat. A palm-leaf bundle and stylus beside it tie the hand to Ramayyan, and no script or pseudo-text is visible. The hand is sound. Minor: the tiny blurred drillers through the window wear white tunics and caps instead of bare chests and topknots. The plain wall in the upper centre (about x 0.42-0.62, y 0-0.3) and the window sky hold the two captions.

Acceptable. De Lannoy matches his sheet's face and hair: pale wavy hair with a black ribbon, in the torn, soot-stained blue coat. The bandage is correctly on his LEFT hand, which is pressed to his chest. His sidelong glance, knit brow and clutching hand read as the flinch. The room matches: timber door, granite walls, mats and a brass lamp. Minor: the background drillers through the window wear white tunics with red headbands and sashes instead of bare chests and forward-tied topknots. The upper wall between his head and the window (about x 0.52-0.73, y 0.02-0.28) is clear for his short balloon.

Minor: the drill yard reads level with the room rather than below the window, and Varma sits beside the window rather than squarely framed in it. Varma matches his sheet: black hair in a knot on his left side, no turban, gold necklaces, cream-and-gold mundu. De Lannoy's bandaged left hand in the torn, soot-stained blue coat hangs in the near foreground. Bare-chested Nair spearmen with topknots drill against green hills. No painted text. Balloons can go in the sky in the window and on the plain granite wall above Varma.

Clean. This is an over-the-shoulder view from behind Varma, who matches his sheet: sleek jet-black hair with a compact knot above the visible LEFT ear, namam, pearl drop, thin waxed moustache, clean chin, gold beads, cream-and-gold cloth, spear at right. De Lannoy stands by the timber door in the torn, soot-stained blue coat with blue breeches and boots. His RIGHT hand grips his lapel and the linen bandage is on his LEFT hand. A small orange-red patch at his right shoulder is coat lining showing through a tear, not blood. The room, window and drilling Nair spearmen match 10.1. There is wide plain granite wall between De Lannoy and the window for both balloons.

Clean. The tight insert shows Ramayyan alone, bowed and not looking up. He is thin with sharp features, a balding head and curly grey-black sides, plain white cloth, no jewellery and no forehead marks. His stylus scores a palm leaf in his lap with fine plain lines only, nothing legible. Both hands are sound (thumb plus four fingers). The plain granite wall at upper right takes all three balloons. Off-panel De Lannoy's tail points to the right edge. The frame is squarer (1312x1199) than the others on the page.

Clean on the hard criteria. De Lannoy matches his sheet and the bible row: pale curled hair tied with a black ribbon, a torn, soot-stained blue coat, dark breeches and boots, and the linen bandage on his LEFT hand. He stands at the window half turned from us. The hills rise beyond, and bare-chested Nair spearmen with topknots drill in the yard. The upper sky is open for the two speeches, and the plain stone sill along the lower right gives a quiet band for the caption. Minor continuity notes: this window opening is much wider than the window in 10.5, the yard shows a tiled shelter and palisade that 10.5 does not, and the door sits on the wall right beside the window. Rejected alternatives: v01 bandages the RIGHT hand (the one on the sill). v02 puts a long white mundu under the coat, which belongs after page 13 panel 4.

This is the newest version and it is acceptable. De Lannoy faces us full on in the torn blue coat, breeches and boots, with the bandage on his LEFT hand, looking toward the door. Varma sits on the platform behind him with his spear in reach: bare-headed, side knot above his LEFT ear, bare-chested, cream mundu with a gold border, gold necklaces, no turban or crest. Nagoji is seen from behind in the doorway: rust-red turban, long curly black hair, cream tunic, red sash, talwar hilt. The tip of his moustache shows, with no beard on the visible cheek, and his gold ear ornament is a flush round stud, not a drop. Remaining faults for the author: (1) The script asks for only the doorframe and the edge of Nagoji's red sash in the near foreground. Instead his whole back, turban and head fill the left third as an over-the-shoulder shot. All three versions do this. It still reads as his point of view and sets up the reverse angle in 11.1. (2) The ear stud is a slightly large round bead. (3) Varma is only moderately small, not 'small' behind De Lannoy. (4) The window here is a modest opening in the far wall, and the yard behind it differs from the wide window and tiled shelter in 10.4. There is low-detail stone wall for the three balloons: upper centre-left between Nagoji's head and De Lannoy, above De Lannoy's head, and upper right of De Lannoy above Varma. Backup v02 has the same composition but adds two unscripted seated men (lower right) and shows the yard spearmen clothed with shields.
decisions.correction: No retouch is needed to use v03. Optional: shrink Nagoji's gold ear bead to a tiny flush stud on the lobe, at about x 0.243, y 0.223 of the frame. The framing fault (Nagoji drawn large instead of just the sash edge) cannot be fixed by a local retouch.

decisions.issues: Minor: Varma in the background is only slightly soft rather than clearly out of focus. Bandage correctly on De Lannoy's left hand (viewer's right, palm up). Upper-left wall, top-centre sky and upper-right wall hold the two balloons and the caption.

Mild continuity jump: De Lannoy kneels on the mat here, but he stands in 11.1 (and through page 10) and is shown standing again in 11.4. It is still readable as him sitting down for the audience. The script beat is met: De Lannoy in profile at frame-left with his head lifted, and Varma seated at frame-right with a slight smile. The bandage is correctly on his far left hand.

Clean apart from one small staging point: Varma looks up and to the left toward De Lannoy, not down at Ramayyan, so the nod to Ramayyan reads only loosely. Everything else checks out. De Lannoy has the torn, soot-stained blue coat, boots and pale hair, his head is bowed in the nod, and the linen bandage is correctly on his LEFT wrist (v02 has it on the right). Ramayyan sits on the mat with his stylus moving on the palm leaf. Varma is bare-headed with the knot above and behind the left ear, the namam, pearl drops and a thin moustache, his spear is within reach and the lamp is brass. There is no painted text. Lettering space: the bare upper wall between the window and Varma (about x 0.53 to 0.80, y 0 to 0.25) and the window sky. v01 is rejected because De Lannoy wears a white mundu and sandals under the coat.

Forced pick, with three faults left. (1) De Lannoy is seen from behind and the linen bandage is on his RIGHT wrist (viewer's right, by the guard's back). The bible puts it on the LEFT, and his bare left hand is visible at the viewer's left of the coat. v02 has the same fault. (2) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold bead sitting slightly below the lobe, not a flush stud. It is smaller than v02's clear stud-plus-drop, which is why v03 wins on this point. (3) Ramayyan wears a tiny gold ear stud, and he should have no jewellery. The rest matches the script beat. De Lannoy's back, in the torn blue coat with boots and pale hair, goes out the door between two bare-chested Nair spearmen. Nagoji stands aside by the wall: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves down, red sash, talwar, boots, thick curled moustache and a clean-shaven chin. Ramayyan looks up from his leaf, and Varma, bare-headed with the side knot, namam and pearls and with his spear beside him, watches the door. There is no painted text. Lettering space: the bare upper granite wall between Nagoji and the window (about x 0.47 to 0.71, y 0 to 0.27) and the window sky. v01 is rejected: Varma has loose curly greying hair, Nagoji's sleeves are rolled up showing the brand, and De Lannoy wears a white skirt.
decisions.correction: A small local pixel retouch would fix all three faults. (a) Paint the white linen wrap off De Lannoy's RIGHT wrist and hand (about x 0.21 to 0.235, y 0.425 to 0.50), continuing the blue coat cuff and the skin of his hand. Then paint a matching narrow linen bandage round his bare LEFT wrist and hand (about x 0.09 to 0.12, y 0.47 to 0.52). (b) Shrink Nagoji's gold ear bead (about x 0.425, y 0.195) to a tiny flat stud flush on the lobe, with nothing below it. (c) Paint out the small gold stud on Ramayyan's earlobe (about x 0.64, y 0.518) in skin tone.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji's sleeves are rolled and the brand plus white scar show on his left forearm, although 12.1 does not call for pushed-up sleeves. The brand reads as a pale ridged patch, with no letters and no cross, and it matches 12.4. The drilling spearmen seen through the window wear red caps where bare-headed Nair topknots were expected. Varma is bare-headed with a knot on the left-rear of his head, holds one finger up, and his spear leans within reach. Nagoji's moustache, clean chin and stud are on model. The upper grey wall between the two men is clear for both Varma balloons.

v03 is essentially clean and keeps the room from 12.1: same timber door on the left, barred window onto green hills and drilling Nair spearmen, mats on the stone platform, brass lamps. Nagoji matches the commander sheet: rust-red turban, red sash, curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, boots, talwar. Varma is bare-headed with the side knot above his LEFT ear, plus namam, pearl drops, gold necklaces and the cream-and-gold mundu. He is half-risen with his hand closed on the spear. Minor points for the author: (1) Varma's moustache is a little thicker and more curled than the thin waxed points on his sheet, though it is the same as in v02 and close to 12.1. (2) Nagoji's left forearm and hand are hidden behind Varma's arm, and Varma's lowered right hand sits right beside Nagoji's scabbard tip, so it can read as almost touching the sword. (3) A brass lamp is lit in daylight, which is allowed. There is no painted text, balloon, blood or anachronism. Lettering space is clear on the plain granite wall: above and to the right of Nagoji's turban (x 0.32-0.50, y 0.02-0.18) for NAGOJI, and between Varma's head and the window (x 0.58-0.78, y 0.02-0.24) for VARMA. Backup v02 is the same composition, but it paints the brand patch on Nagoji's RIGHT forearm (visible at lower left), which is the wrong arm, and the script does not call for it here.

Clean, with minor notes only. The front prisoner's shirt has earthy brown stains that read as grime, not blood. A tiny metal cup sits on a shelf inside the far-left doorway; it is negligible. Nagoji is correct: curled moustache, clean chin, stud, and the brand on his inner LEFT forearm (sleeves pushed up). Varma is correct: bare-headed, left-side knot, namam, pearl drops. The Nair guards and the prisoners eating from leaves in the lower yard match the script, the light is hard noon, and the wide sky gives ample caption space.

Minor. The background courtyard is a two-storey galleried block with a stair, a little grander than the single-storey tiled quarters in 12.3. The upper-left sky band is fairly tight for four lettering areas, so the long Nagoji line may need the low-detail flagstones at the lower left. Everything else matches. The light is pre-dawn blue-grey. De Lannoy is tall with pale wavy hair and a black ribbon, wears the torn soot-stained blue coat and boots, and has the linen bandage on his LEFT hand and wrist. On the stone bench by his door sit a folded white tunic-coat, a folded white mundu and sandals. Nagoji arrives across the flagstones in the commander look with his sleeves pushed up. His brand is a pale puckered patch beside a thin white scar, with no letters. His chin is clean and he has a small gold stud. There is no painted text.

Acceptable. It is a tight shot of De Lannoy with his RIGHT thumb on the brass buttons, which carry interlaced marks but no letters. The linen bandage is on his LEFT hand and wrist. The coat is torn and soot-stained, with pale hair and a black ribbon, set in the pre-dawn blue-grey courtyard that matches 12.4. One small note: the bandage carries brown grime stains, while it looked cleaner in 12.4. The stain colour is earthy brown and does not read as blood. The long balloon fits in the upper-right sky and hills, clear of his face and hands.

Minor only: Nagoji gestures with his outstretched arm toward the hills instead of nodding past De Lannoy. Otherwise clean. Pre-dawn blue-grey light with lit oil lamps. De Lannoy wears the torn blue coat, with the bandage on his left hand. Nagoji is clean-shaven, with a thick curled moustache and a flush gold stud. His sleeves are pushed up, and the brand and scar sit correctly on the inner LEFT forearm on the side of the talwar. There is open sky above and between the heads for both balloons.

Minor: the whole courtyard is in warm sunlight, where the script asks for first light only catching the wall tops, and De Lannoy fills more of the frame than a wide, still panel suggests. He is on model: torn, soot-stained blue coat, plain brass buttons with no letters, the bandage correctly on his LEFT hand, quietly unbuttoning. The courtyard and stone bench match 12.4, and there is no painted text.

Minor only: the folded torn blue coat sits on the bench at mid-right rather than in the true foreground, and the light is warm low sun instead of a cooler first light. Otherwise this matches the script and bible. He is barefoot in a stained shirt open at the throat, holding the white mundu up like a map, with the bandage on his LEFT hand and the boots set beside the bench. The sky upper left and upper centre is clear for the short balloon.

v03 is the newest version and is nearly clean. Both men match their sheets. De Lannoy has pale hair tied with a black ribbon, the white tunic-coat over an ankle-length white mundu, sandals, and the bandage on his LEFT hand in both the inset and the main image. Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, a clean chin, a small gold stud on the lobe, the rust-red turban, the red waist sash with no shoulder cloth, sleeves pushed up and the talwar on his left hip. The upper-left inset is a faceless crop of the tuck: Nagoji's hands guide the cloth, a single brand shows on his forearm, and the cloth end hangs from De Lannoy's bandaged hand. The folded blue coat lies on the stone bench, and the courtyard matches 13.3. Remaining faults: (1) In the main image the pale brand patch and the white scar are drawn on Nagoji's outstretched RIGHT forearm, the arm on the viewer's left, palm up. The bible puts them on the inner LEFT forearm only, and this main image does not need them at all. They are small but visible at print size. (2) His boots from 13.3 are missing beside the coat on the bench, a minor continuity slip. (3) There is little room for lettering. The sky band is narrow, so both main speeches ("Do I look ridiculous?" and Nagoji's medium reply) have to share the sky and the plain grey wall between the two heads (about x 0.50 to 0.76, y 0.00 to 0.32). The oath goes just below the inset over the roof tiles (about x 0.01 to 0.15, y 0.29 to 0.37). It is workable without covering faces or hands. (4) The tuck itself is hidden under the tunic-coat in the main image; only De Lannoy's hand at the waist suggests it. Backup v02 has the same composition but the same right-forearm brand, two brands on Nagoji's two inset forearms, and a weaker grip on the sword hilt.
decisions.correction: A small local retouch fixes the worst fault. In the main image, paint out the pale rosette brand and the thin white scar on Nagoji's outstretched forearm (the palm-up arm reaching toward De Lannoy). They sit at roughly x 1025 to 1095 px, y 395 to 470 px of the 1536 x 1024 frame (fractions x 0.67 to 0.71, y 0.39 to 0.46). Fill that area with the surrounding forearm skin tone and shading. Leave the single brand in the upper-left inset unchanged.

decisions.issues: Framing differs: the script asks for a shot over De Lannoy's shoulder, but this is a side-by-side two-shot, and Nagoji points at the yard instead of nodding. The beat still reads. Nagoji looks stern and indicates the Nair squad gathering in the lower yard, with a Nair captain at its head. Bible details are correct. De Lannoy wears the white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals, with the bandage on his LEFT hand. Nagoji is clean-shaven, with a moustache and stud, and the brand is on his inner LEFT forearm on the talwar side. Small points: the squad's topknots sit on the crown rather than tied forward, the captain wears a red sash, and the light is fuller daylight than early light. The large sky upper right takes Nagoji's two balloons. De Lannoy's short balloon can sit in the sky between the two heads.

Minor issues only. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold ball at the lobe, close to a stud but not perfectly flush. His sleeves are rolled as on the commander sheet, so the pale brand patch and thin scar show on his inner left forearm, although the script does not call for it. The light reads as full morning rather than growing light. Otherwise the panel is clean. It is a two-shot in the Udayagiri courtyard with steps to the upper walk, tiled roofs, a stone bench and green hills. Nagoji (turban, sash, curled moustache, clean chin) gestures as he speaks. De Lannoy, in white mundu and tunic-coat with the bandage on his left hand, listens. There is no painted text, and open sky in the upper centre and upper left leaves room for both balloons.

Minor issues only. The shot is medium-full rather than a close-up, so the faint shift in his face reads as a dry, unsmiling stare without much nuance. He looks frame-right, which reverses his eyeline from 14.1, so the off-panel Nagoji tail goes to the right edge. The panel matches the sheet: pale hair tied with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat and mundu, and the bandage on his left hand and wrist. It is the same courtyard as 14.1, the hands are sound, there is no text, and a wide band of sky at the upper right leaves room for both balloons.

De Lannoy fills about two thirds of the frame height rather than reading as a small figure. He is still clearly alone against a wide view of the amber sky and the country below. Otherwise the panel matches the script and sheet: white mundu, tunic-coat and sandals, the bandage on his left hand, and no coat anywhere. He walks the granite wall walk at evening with palm groves, paddy and the sea beyond. The hands and feet are sound, there is no text, and the large sky in the upper half takes all three captions.

Minor issues only. The small, distant De Lannoy has white bandage wraps on both wrists; the bible has the bandage on his left only. At this size it reads almost as white cuffs. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold bead at the lobe, not a perfectly flush stud, and his jaw has slight stipple shading. The parapet geometry where the foreground block meets the receding wall is a little ambiguous. The beat works: Nagoji (turban, sash, curled moustache, clean chin) lays his left palm flat on the granite parapet at dusk, with the brand and long scar on his inner left forearm as the bible gives them. De Lannoy's small white figure stands far along the same rampart. There is no text, and open dusk sky at the upper left and across the top leaves room for both captions.

The bastions carry small domed stone sentry turrets that look somewhat like European garitas. The prompt asked for no European towers, and the bastions in 14.3 and 14.4 have no such turrets. These are small and read as generic fort turrets, so the panel is still acceptable. Otherwise it is clean: a wide 3:1 dusk vista of the granite ramparts with the green country of palm groves and paddy running from the hills to the sea, matching the light and landscape of 14.3 and 14.4. There are no figures and no text, and a broad band of open sky across the top takes the long caption.

about_r3: Identity fixes (2026-10-08 sheets and bible markers): edits of the audited frame accepted by v15-identity-verify. page-07-panel-05: The whole frame was lightly re-rendered: skin and textures are a little smoother and softer everywhere, but composition, framing, the runner, the lancers, Kayal and the Dutch are unchanged. The jaw stubble stipple of v01 is gone, which helps the clean-shaven chin. The flush lobe stud now reads slightly paler, close to pearl-toned, but it is still a single flush stud with nothing hanging below. At 3x zoom both forearms are plain unmarked skin with tendons; the right hand grips the talwar and the left hand holds the reins, both drawn cleanly. page-12-panel-01: These are NOTE-level and the same in v01: Nagoji's lobe stud has a small second bead just below it (about 4 px). His inner LEFT forearm brand is a pale ridged vertical patch with a white scar beside it, with no letters or cross. The frame was lightly re-rendered overall (smoother skin, less jaw stipple on Nagoji), but there is no composition change, Nagoji's face is the same, and Varma's raised finger and resting hand are drawn cleanly.
